subject: Revolving credit + VAT reserve proposal — Novamed
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@novamed.io>, accounts-pay <accounts-pay@novamed.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: revolving credit corridor + VAT reserve for initial deployment

Hi Ana / Novamed AP team —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a concise proposal for a short-term credit corridor and an EU VAT evidence holdback that lets you run the pilot while we keep exposure limited. High-level points: 

- Term: pilot invoice cadence for first 90 days; monthly invoices.
- Net terms: Net45 standard for host invoices; Net60 on milestone fees if Novamed requires commercial breathing room.
- Revolving credit corridor: capped at €120k for pilot; triggers a review at 75% utilization.
- VAT reserve: 12% holdback on cross-border service lines until customer provides VAT registration / reverse charge evidence for EU entity (or we route to Novamed EU invoicing entity).
- Early-payment incentive: 1.0% on invoice if paid within 10 days (applies if Net45 accepted).
- Security: optional short-term escrow or performance deposit (we recommend a single-month prepay if Novamed prefers no escrow).

I've attached the draft SOW and a sample invoice schedule. This is intentionally conservative and intended to accelerate procurement / PO issuance while we finalize tax flows. Please confirm which path you prefer (Net45 + VAT holdback vs Net60 + reduced holdback) so we can update the SOW and DocuSign.

Next steps: if Net45 + 12% reserve is acceptable, I will: 1) add the clause to the SOW, 2) issue the DocuSign packet, and 3) provision the reserved capacity.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: Redwood_Draft_SOW_v3.pdf, Proposed_Invoice_Schedule.xlsx, KYC-checklist.docx

From: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@novamed.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: accounts-pay <accounts-pay@novamed.io>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:08:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Proposal: revolving credit corridor + VAT reserve for initial deployment

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the note and the materials. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Novamed legal / tax are likely to request Net60 for the initial PO (internal policy aligned with our Q2 cashflow plan). 
- On VAT: we cannot produce EU reverse-charge evidence for the UK entity immediately; we can route invoices to our DE subsidiary (Novamed GmbH) but that will require intercompany steps and a change to the bill-to.
- Holdback: 12% is a bit high for us for the pilot. Would Redwood accept an 8% temporary VAT reserve if we commit to route invoicing to Novamed GmbH for subsequent invoices once the PO is in place?

We are sympathetic to Redwood's exposure concerns and open to the early-pay discount if Net45 can be negotiated. Can you confirm whether the reserve is refundable at first formal compliance pass and how quickly refunds are processed? Also please include any language in the SOW that allows invoice reissue when bill-to changes to the DE entity.

Best,
Ana Gomez
Director, Finance Operations
Novamed
ana.gomez@novamed.io
+44 20 7946 0211

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: revolving credit corridor + VAT reserve for initial deployment

Folks —

Thoughts on risk / remedy options if Novamed asks for Net60 and an 8% reserve: 

- Approve Net60 only with an increased revolving cap hold: bump to €160k and short-term credit review at 50% utilization. This balances their cashflow ask with our exposure.
- Refund cadence: once Novamed provides valid DE invoicing and VAT evidence we reissue the affected invoice(s) and process a refund of the reserve within 14 calendar days. Include SLA in SOW.
- Escrow vs deposit: escrow adds friction; recommend a one-month prepay (applies to first month of committed capacity) if they insist on Net60. Prepay protects Redwood and is easier operationally.

If we can get Net60 + 8% reserve + one-month prepay OR Net45 + 8% reserve (no prepay), I'd accept the commercial tradeoff. Also suggest a clause capping cumulative outstanding at the revolving corridor (no surprises).

I can draft the SOW language: refund SLA, reserve unwind process, and invoicing reissue clause.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: revolving credit corridor + VAT reserve for initial deployment

Rafael / Kim —

I ran numbers on the two compromise pathways: Net45 + 8% reserve vs Net60 + 8% reserve + one-month prepay. Key takeaways: 

- Expected receivables exposure (90-day pilot): Net45 + 8% reserve = ~€88k average exposure; Net60 + prepay = ~€65k (because prepay offsets month 1).
- Revenue recognition & tax: if we reissue to DE entity we must ensure VAT is not double-charged; legal needs to approve rerouting clause.
- Suggested credit limit language: automatic review at 50% usage, mandatory finance sync if >75% usage, and hard stop at 100% until remedial measures agreed.

Operational asks for SOW: include the refund SLA (14 days), template for invoice reissue, PO / bill-to update flow, and a short KYC checklist (I attached it). If Novamed agrees to a one-month prepay for Net60 we can accept the longer terms with the 8% reserve. Otherwise push for Net45 + 8%.

I'll prep a redline for the SOW and the invoice schedule; Rafael, if you want I can include the refund SLA language and an example timeline for reserve release.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: KYC-checklist.docx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@novamed.io>, accounts-pay <accounts-pay@novamed.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: revolving credit corridor + VAT reserve for initial deployment

Ana —

Thanks for the quick reply and for surfacing the routing requirement. To summarize the mutually acceptable path Redwood can commit to today: 

1) Commercial: Net60 with an 8% temporary VAT reserve for the pilot period, conditional on a one-month prepay credited to the first invoice OR Net45 with an 8% reserve and no prepay.
2) Credit corridor: increase to €160k if Net60 path selected (review at 50% usage).
3) Refund / reissue: we will reissue invoices to Novamed GmbH and process reserve refunds within 14 calendar days of receiving valid VAT/bill-to evidence. This will be codified in SOW.
4) Operational: we will provide a short invoice-reissue checklist and the DocuSign SOW once you confirm which commercial path you prefer.

Can you confirm by end of day Wednesday which option you prefer? Once we have that, I'll circulate an updated SOW and the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.
Rafael
